findings.title: Russian State-Supported Cyber Actors Conduct Phishing Campaign Targeting Users of Zimbra Collaboration Suite (CISA AA26-204A)
findings.summary_md: Joint advisory from CISA, FBI, NSA, and 13+ international partners confirms LAUNDRY BEAR (also Void Blizzard / CL-STA-1114) has exploited CVE-2025-66376 in Zimbra Collaboration Suite since July 2025. The zero-click XSS exploit requires only viewing a malicious email and exfiltrates 90 days of email, passwords, 2FA tokens, GAL, and newly created application passcodes. The vulnerability was patched in November 2025 (ZCS 10.1.13 and 10.0.18) but exploitation continues against unpatched instances.

findings.title: Russian Global Webmail Espionage - Unit 42 (CL-STA-1114)
findings.summary_md: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 details the CL-STA-1114 campaign using a zero-click Zimbra XSS (CVE-2025-66376) that started in July 2025. The payload uses an invisible SVG with Base64-encoded and XOR-encrypted JavaScript to collect CSRF tokens, email archives, 2FA scratch codes, environment details, and organization directories. Nine C2 IP addresses and nine domains (e.g., zmailanalytics.com, zimbra-metadata.com) were observed, with servers active for an average of 35.4 days.
